sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four statements or pairs of ½ mark (true/false, match the columns, fill in the blanks or arrange in sequence).

questions.q: State True or False: (i) Values are learnt from parents and surroundings. (ii) Ethics test our values. (iii) Rights and responsibilities go together. (iv) Expressing your views respectfully is your right.
questions.answer: (i) True. (ii) True. (iii) True. (iv) False – expressing views is a right but doing it respectfully is a duty.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Your conscience is your internal ______. (ii) Respect must be ______ to be received. (iii) ______ labour means respecting all jobs equally. (iv) Tolerance of ______ things is a great evil.

Match the person with the value: (i) Asif the taxi driver (ii) Mrs Gill (iii) The little boy with the puppy (iv) Krishna the cobbler; (a) empathy (b) honesty (c) dignity of labour (d) positive attitude.

State True or False: (i) Caring for others depends on our mood. (ii) Education and good upbringing promote values. (iii) Children from poor families cannot have values. (iv) Tolerance and empathy are keys to a peaceful life.
Which of these are signs of disrespect? (i) Greeting everyone in the room (ii) Going out without informing your mother (iii) Raising your voice with elders (iv) Introducing friends to the family.
questions.answer: (ii) and (iii) are signs of disrespect; (i) and (iv) are signs of respect.

questions.q: Fill in the blanks: (i) Life skills help to improve the ______ of life. (ii) 'Adaptive' means a person is ______ in approach. (iii) A positive attitude brings ______ and avoids negative thinking. (iv) The cobbler Krishna wanted to earn his meal in a ______ manner.

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What can be the four consequences of not following values in the society?
questions.answer: Loss of life and damage to public property; crime and corruption; breakdown of families and loss of law and order; alcohol and drug abuse; abuse of women, children and vulnerable people; wastage of resources.

questions.q: List any four essential values that help to maintain a conducive atmosphere at home.
questions.answer: Honesty and loyalty; respect for work; punctuality, regularity and discipline; courtesy and politeness; judicious use of resources; taking initiative; efficiency in completing tasks.

questions.q: Mention any four expected ethics in a nurse.
questions.answer: Honesty and truthfulness; punctuality and regularity; empathy and care for patients; courtesy and politeness; respect for work and confidentiality; efficiency in completing tasks.

questions.q: Define values and ethics with one example.
questions.answer: Values are the ideas and beliefs we hold as important and learn from parents and surroundings, e.g. caring for others. Ethics are the way we behave in difficult situations that test our values, e.g. the taxi driver returning the briefcase he found.

questions.q: Why is dignity of labour important?
questions.answer: All jobs are respected equally; respectability lies in how well work is done, not its kind; it encourages people to earn their living honestly instead of depending on others or begging.

questions.q: How can we show respect to our elders? (any four)
questions.answer: Greet them; take leave of them; introduce friends to them; speak politely and avoid a raised voice; inform them before going out; consider their wishes while using the TV; disagree politely.

questions.q: Write two good manners in conversation.
questions.answer: Do not interrupt when two people are talking; converse in a language understood by all; speak cheerfully and think before speaking.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: What is the importance of ethics in our daily life? Explain.
questions.answer: Values and ethics are the base of our actions and behaviour. If they are practised there is peace, law and order and respect for rights and responsibilities. Without them there will be crime, corruption, breakdown of families, drug abuse, abuse of the vulnerable and wastage of resources, so it is each person's responsibility to live ethically; at the workplace ethics (honesty, punctuality, loyalty, courtesy) create a conducive atmosphere.

questions.q: Explain tolerance, empathy and positive attitude with one example each.
questions.answer: Tolerance is the ability to accept opinions and practices different from our own (but not injustice or corruption). Empathy is the capacity to recognise and share the feelings of others – the little boy chose the limping puppy so that it would not be lonely. A positive attitude brings optimism and helps to cope with daily life – Mrs Gill pointed out one good quality in each of her naughty students and they became achievers.

questions.q: Describe the values of life that help to maintain a good atmosphere in the family (any six).
questions.answer: Honesty and loyalty; respect for work; punctuality, regularity and discipline; courtesy and politeness; judicious use of resources; taking initiative; efficiency in completing tasks.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: Explain the signs of showing respect and disrespect to elders and five good manners.
questions.answer: Disrespect: not greeting everyone in a room; not taking leave of elders; not introducing friends to the family; raising the voice in arguments; going out without informing or changing the TV channel without caring for others; staying away on important family days. Respect: greeting everyone, taking leave, introducing friends, speaking politely, informing elders. Good manners: speak cheerfully; think before you speak; do not interrupt; never speak ill of others; speak in a language understood by all; be humble; do not whisper in a group.

questions.q: Explain dignity of labour with examples and why we should not depend on others.
questions.answer: Dignity of labour means that all work, manual or intellectual, is respected equally and no occupation is considered superior; respectability lies in doing the work well. Krishna the cobbler worked at 70 to earn his meal in a dignified manner; the Prophet asked a beggar to cut and sell wood; Guru Nanak preferred the dry bread earned by honest labour. It is better to earn one's living honestly than to depend on others.
